steps.narration: By the end of this walkthrough, Velox will be watching every requirement in your BRD against the Jira story it produced. To start, open the Drift Alignment Tab from the left rail and choose Docs Sync.
Docs Sync opens on the BRD to Jira tab, where two queues run in opposite directions.
Open the traceability panel. Velox only watches a requirement once it is linked to a story, and linking it is a one-time setup.
With no BRD yet, generate it and its stories together in the BRD Assistant, where the links are created as the items are generated.

beats.caption: Generate the BRD and its stories

steps.narration: Or with the BRD already in Confluence, let the agent propose a matching story for each requirement instead.
Pick the BRD page from Confluence. Confirming it sets the agent matching each requirement against the stories that already exist.
Matching combines embeddings-based similarity with the model's own judgment, and takes about a minute.
Results land in three buckets, and each one asks something different of you.
Recommended holds the confident matches, each with the top story already ticked and a written rationale beside its confidence score.

beats.caption: Recommended Bucket: Confident matches, top story pre-selected

steps.narration: A label says how strong the match is, and partial is a normal outcome rather than a near miss.
Needs review bucket leaves the choice to you, with nothing pre-selected. Tick the right story and the confirm count moves with it.

beats.caption: Needs review Bucket: Pick the story yourself

steps.narration: Coverage gaps are requirements with no story behind them yet, and Velox explains why nothing matched.

beats.caption: Coverage Gaps: Requirements with no story yet

steps.narration: Confirming switches drift detection on for exactly the pairs you ticked, for continuous monitoring

beats.caption: Detection on for the linked pairs

steps.narration: Changes to apply carries a requirement's new wording toward its story. Drift to resolve works the other way.
Drift to resolve reads comments as well as fields, so a comment implying a scope change is flagged before the story itself changes.

beats.caption: Comments are flagged, not just edits

steps.narration: Open a pending change and the current story sits beside the proposed one, with a confidence score on the proposal.

beats.caption: Current story beside the proposed one

steps.narration: The Agent Rationale says why the change was drafted, and you can approve it, edit it first, or dismiss it. Approving only queues it.
The change reaches Jira when you apply the batch, which is a second and deliberate action.

beats.caption: Apply the batch to reach Jira

steps.narration: Back on the page, the flagged items on the right are the ones Jira changed without the BRD catching up.
Open one and the BRD source sits beside the current story, which is often much longer than the requirement it came from.

beats.caption: Source beside current, side by side

steps.narration: You decide which side is right. Say the BRD is behind, say the story is wrong, or accept that the difference was meant.
Accepting the drift stops the pair being flagged, and an optional note leaves the reason for whoever reads it next.

beats.caption: Accept the drift, leave a note

steps.narration: Resolving updates the list straight away and the flagged count drops. Every pair you linked stays watched from here, in both directions.

variants.note: Baseline. Tutorials carry no hook or cta.
